meta: Business flooding, overflowing floor drains or a failed backflow test? Commercial plumbing in Oakley, CA, day or night. Clear price first. Call (888) 910-8644.
lead: Commercial plumbing in Oakley, CA covers the leaks, drain overflows, grease traps and backflow tests that keep a shop, restaurant or office open. We answer after-hours calls as well as scheduled ones.
If water is on the floor of your business right now, start with the steps just below.
intro: Commercial plumbing is the repair, testing and maintenance of the supply, drain and protective devices in non-residential buildings. It differs from home work because of larger lines, floor drains, grease interceptors and backflow assemblies that the water utility may track.

Oakley's business areas include the Laurel Road corridor with Laurel Plaza, and Cypress Square on Main Street. This page covers emergency steps, business-hours versus after-hours work, leak detection, backflow testing, grease traps, storm drains and property manager questions.

sections.h2: Water or sewage on the floor of your business
paras: A flooding break room or an overflowing floor drain can close a business for the day. Our 24/7 emergency dispatch takes commercial calls at any hour, and these steps limit the damage and protect people while you wait.
do_now: Keep customers and staff away from standing water, and treat sewage as a health hazard.
Find the building's main shutoff and close it if the water is clean and still flowing.
Switch off power to affected equipment, kitchen gear and outlets at the panel only if you can reach it dry.
Stop using sinks, toilets and floor drains that feed the affected line.
Move stock, files and electronics off the floor and photograph the damage.
If you rent, tell your landlord or property manager right away and keep their name and time of contact.

paras: Many commercial faults are not flooding, so waiting until morning may be sensible. The table shows how we usually split the two, but you decide based on your risk.

sections.h2: Safety steps for staff while you wait for a plumber
paras: Staff on site can limit harm in the first minutes. Do not let anyone walk through standing water near outlets or equipment, and avoid using a toilet or sink that is backing up.
Shut off the water at the building main if you know where it is, document the damage with photos for the landlord and the insurer, and close the area to customers.
Businesses near Main Street can read the [[plumber-downtown-oakley-ca|Downtown Oakley page]] for how tenants and landlords usually split responsibility.
bullets: Move people away from wet floors and any area where sewage is rising
Switch off power to wet equipment only if the panel is dry and you can reach it safely
Gas smell: evacuate, call 911 and PG&E at 1-800-743-5000 before any plumber
Tell dispatch whether the building is leased and who can approve the work

sections.h2: Finding a leak in a commercial building
paras: Commercial leak detection works the same way it does in a home. We close fixtures, watch the meter, pressure test sections of pipe and listen for the sound of water in slab or wall lines. That is enough for many shops, offices and small restaurants.

We are honest about limits. Fire mains, large irrigation systems and big multi-building sites can need specialists with their own equipment, and we will say so after the first visit rather than keep billing. If a leak sits between the street and your meter, it is Diablo Water District's side, so ask the district to confirm. We also work with businesses in nearby [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood]]. For related methods, see our [[leak-detection|leak detection]] page.

sections.h2: Backflow testing and your water utility
paras: A backflow assembly stops used or contaminated water from flowing backward into the public supply. Diablo Water District tests more than 4,500 backflow devices a year, so utility notices about annual testing are routine for businesses with irrigation, fire lines or certain equipment.

If you received a notice, read the deadline and the device location on it. Ask Diablo Water District at (925) 625-3798 what happens after a missed test and how it wants results reported, since those details come from the district, not us. We test and repair or replace assemblies, and we can handle a group of devices in one visit.
Commercial installs and backflow work follow the California Plumbing Code, the state's version of the UPC published by IAPMO, and a business should ask for that in writing on any quote.
A grease trap catches fat before it reaches the sewer, and it works only if it is emptied before it fills. Restaurants and bakeries see slow drains, odors and backups when the trap is overdue.

We clean and inspect the trap and the lines leading to it. Large interceptors are often pumped by a hauler, and we will tell you which one yours needs. If grease causes an overflow from your private line, the owner is responsible for cleanup and damage, so a regular schedule is cheaper than a backup.

sections.h2: Storm drains and parking-lot catch basins
paras: Catch basins and storm drains collect leaves, silt and trash from lots and loading areas. When they clog, rain collects at doors and in dips, and winter storms expose weak spots quickly.

We clear blockages with jetting and a camera, and we check for broken pipe or poor slope. For heavy blockages see [[hydro-jetting|hydro jetting]], and ask the City of Oakley whether a drain you share with a neighbor is yours.

sections.h2: Floor drains and drain overflows in commercial space
paras: A floor drain that overflows is a symptom, not the problem itself. These are the usual reasons.

items.d: Kitchens, car wash bays and shops send solids that settle in the trap.
If several drains back up at once, the building's main drain is involved. [[sewer-line-cleaning|Sewer line cleaning]] clears it.
A basement or low fixture may use a pump that has stopped.
A rarely used drain can smell because its water seal evaporated.

paras: Business jobs vary a great deal, so we explain the scope first. For a business, the price is agreed in advance, which helps when a manager must approve the work order.

factors.d: Larger pipe, multiple restrooms or kitchen lines take more time.
Night work and jobs that must avoid public hours are priced differently.
Backflow assemblies need testing, tags and sometimes repair parts.
Who pays under your lease affects who authorizes the work.
Old pipe, shared lines and clogged interceptors may add steps.

sections.insurance: Commercial property policies often cover sudden water damage but not gradual leaks or maintenance failures. Photograph the loss, keep invoices and call your insurer before major repairs.
sections.call_line: Call (888) 910-8644 with the building type and the symptom, and we will give you the real number.

faqs.q: Do you handle commercial plumbing emergencies at night or on weekends in Oakley?
a: Yes. Dispatch runs 24/7 and takes business calls at any hour, including nights, weekends and holidays.

faqs.q: As a property manager, can you take work orders for several tenants?
a: Yes. Send the building, unit, contact and symptom, and tell us who authorizes the spend. We can keep separate invoices per unit.

faqs.q: As a landlord, who pays for a plumbing repair in a leased space?
a: That depends on your lease, not on us. We document the cause and the location so you and the tenant can sort out responsibility.

faqs.q: What is a backflow test and how often is it needed?
a: It checks that the assembly stops water from flowing backward. Ask Diablo Water District how often it requires tests for your device and where results go.

faqs.q: Can you pump and clean a grease trap?
a: We clean and inspect traps and their lines. Large interceptors may need a hauler, and we tell you before work starts.

faqs.q: Why does my floor drain overflow?
a: Usually debris, grease or a blocked main line. If several drains react together, the building's drain is likely involved.

faqs.q: Is my business sewer lateral in Oakley the owner's responsibility?
a: Yes. Private lateral maintenance belongs to the property owner, while The public sewer is run by Ironhouse Sanitary District. Call (925) 625-2279 to confirm the boundary.

cta_mid: If your business has water on the floor, shut the main and give dispatch the building address and what is affected.
cta_end: Leaking line, overflowing drain or backflow notice at your Oakley business, send the details and we will schedule it.
